kings-island: The linked Guest Accessibility Guide lists car and van spaces in the main lots, first come, first served, with a valid disability placard or plate displayed. Ask at the parking toll booths for directions. If those spaces are full, it identifies a passenger drop-off near the main entrance.

Accessible parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis within the main parking lots of the park. When you arrive at the parking toll booths, ask an Associate for instructions regarding where to proceed to the accessible parking lot. Both auto and van accessible spaces are provided. A valid disabled persons parking placard or license plate must be displayed at all times while parked in the designated accessible parking area. If the designated accessible parking area is full at the time of your arrival, members of your party may be dropped off at the main pick-up/drop-off area, near the main entrance to the park.

The guide lists adult changing tables at the Family Care Center, near the Coconut Cove restroom, and in family restrooms inside the Front Gate and at Queen City Stunt Coaster, Invertigo and Banshee. It does not supply table dimensions or weight limits.
Adult changing tables are located at the Family Care Center, near the Coconut Cove restroom, and the following family restrooms: inside Front Gate, Queen City Stunt Coaster, Invertigo, and Banshee.

The guide lists private restrooms for visitors who need another person’s assistance at every restroom location, including First Aid, and wheelchair-accessible stalls in all restrooms. These are the park’s descriptions, not measured layouts.

Private restroom facilities for Guest needing the assistance of another Guest are available at all restroom locations throughout the park, including First Aid. Wheelchair accessible stalls are located at all restrooms.

The First Aid building in Planet Snoopy beside Charlie Brown’s Wind Up is listed as staffed from park opening to closing, with medical-equipment storage and medication refrigeration. A second First Aid location near the Soak City train station operates during Soak City hours.

Our First Aid Building located in PLANET SNOOPY™(adjacent to Charlie Brown’s Wind Up) is staffed from park open to park close. Medical equipment storage and refrigeration for Guests with medication is offered at First Aid. In addition, a First Aid Building is located in Soak City near the T rain Station. This location is open during Soak City operating hours.

The Rental Center is on the left just inside the Front Gate. The guide lists limited wheelchairs, ECVs and strollers, advance online wheelchair/ECV reservations, and on-site rentals while supplies last.

A limited supply of wheelchairs, electric convenience vehicles (ECV), and strollers are available for rent at the Rental Center on the left, just inside the front gate. Online reservations are available for wheelchair/ECV rentals in advance of your visit. Reservations can be made by going to sixflags.com/kingsisland and visit the rentals page under the Tickets tab. Rentals are also available at the park while supplies last.

Rented wheelchairs, ECVs and strollers may not leave the park gates or go to the parking lot. The guide offers staff help at that point but does not define a parking-lot wheelchair service; confirm how to reach or leave the rental counter.
Wheelchairs, ECV’s, and strollers may not be taken out of the park gates or to the parking lot. However, a park Associate will be happy to provide any assistance you may need at that time.

Kings Island says staff are not trained or permitted to transfer guests from wheelchairs into ride vehicles. It asks visitors to bring someone who can physically help when needed; transfer devices do not imply staff lifting assistance.

Kings Island personnel are not trained in transferring Guests from wheelchairs to ride units and are not permitted to do so. Y ou should plan your visit with someone who can physically help you when necessary.

The guide identifies wheelchair lifts to upper ride platforms at Banshee, Mystic Timbers and Orion. Use the call button at the base to request service. It describes manual-wheelchair alternatives where posted lift capacity or ECV attachments prevent use; ask staff about the particular device and lift.

A wheelchair lift is available at Banshee, Mystic Timbers, and Orion to transport a Guest in a wheelchair to our second-story ride platform. Please use the call button at base of lift to request service. Manual wheelchairs are available at all locations with a wheelchair lift if weight exceeds the max posted capacity. If an ECV has attachments to the vehicle which could impede with the operation of a lift or with safe lift ingress and egress, please transfer to manual wheelchair. Applicable attachments would include canopies, antennae, umbrellas, awnings, etc. Please ask an Associate at each location for assistance.

For water-wheelchair or pool-lift access, the guide directs visitors to the Aquatics Supervisory team. It lists water-wheelchair entry assistance at Coconut Cove, Splash River’s entry area, Tidal Wave Bay and Breakers Bay; the chair can be shared by multiple guests during the day. The guide also sets water-depth and rider criteria; ask the team which apply to the intended attraction.

A water wheelchair is available for Guests requiring additional assistance when gaining access into Coconut Cove, Splash River (Entry Area), Tidal Wave Bay, and Breakers Bay. The water wheelchair may be used by multiple Guests on the same day.
During your visit, please speak to a member of our Aquatics Supervisory team to obtain access to the water wheelchair or pool lift and for further accessibility information.

While in a/the wave pool, the water level may not exceed the height of the seat on the chair. Guests participating in a wave pool are permitted to use a personal wheelchair. Personal wheelchairs are permitted up to the seat's water depth. Guests utilizing wheelchairs will not be required to utilize a lifejacket while in the wave pool only if their height exceeds 52" tall and meet all other rider criteria for the attraction.

In order to participate on most attractions, Guests must have independent seated postural control, appropriate center of gravity, appropriated observed behavior, and the ability to enter and exit the attraction safely.
